Class RankingScreen

java.lang.Object
it.polimi.ingsw.client.ui.tui.screen.RankingScreen
public class RankingScreen extends Object
TUI screen that displays the global leaderboard for matches played with a specific number of players. Players are ranked by their cumulative Points in descending order, with ties broken alphabetically by nickname. The top three positions are highlighted with medal colors and emoji. The screen blocks until the player presses Backspace to return to the previous view.

  • Method Details

    • display

      public void display() throws IOException
      Renders the ranking screen and blocks until the player presses Backspace. Saves and restores the terminal state and attributes around the display.
      Throws:
      IOException - if a terminal I/O error occurs

    • saveTerminalState

      private void saveTerminalState()
      Saves the terminal state by hiding the cursor.

    • restoreTerminalState

      private void restoreTerminalState()
      Restores the terminal state by making the cursor visible and resetting ANSI styles.

    • renderScreen

      public void renderScreen()
      Initializes the screen and color buffers to match the current terminal dimensions, writes the title, the ranking table (or an empty state message if no entries are available), and the footer prompt into them, then flushes the result to the terminal. Tied players share the same rank; ranks are assigned by position after sorting.

      Public so it can be re-invoked by the owning ViewTUI on a terminal resize while this screen is being displayed, keeping it visible and correctly sized instead of being silently replaced by a redraw of the main game layout.

    • printAt

      private void printAt(int row, int col, String text, org.jline.utils.AttributedStyle style)
      Writes the given text into the screen and color buffers at the specified position, clipping any characters that fall outside the terminal width.
      Parameters:
      row - the zero-based row index to write at
      col - the zero-based column index to start writing from
      text - the text to write
      style - the ANSI style to apply to the written characters

    • flushBuffers

      private void flushBuffers()
      Flushes the screen and color buffers to the terminal, applying run-length style compression to minimize ANSI escape sequences. Clears any remaining content below the rendered area.

    • waitForBackspace

      private void waitForBackspace()
      Blocks the current thread until the player presses Backspace (ASCII 8 or 127). Any other key press is ignored.
